idea: Report skewness g1=m3/(m2^1.5) and excess kurtosis g2=m4/m2^2-3 for per-vehicle travel time/speed/delay distributions, with test that g1 ~ N(0, sqrt(6/n)); flags when mean-based CIs/t-tests are unreliable and when to use median.
does: Skewness, kurtosis, CV, quartiles/IQR and normality flag for any run metric
outputs: g1, g2, CV, IQR, z of skew, advice (use median/log)
notes: Cheap addition to analyse_run; also CV as relative dispersion across scenarios.

idea: Spearman rs=1-6*sum(d^2)/(n(n^2-1)) as nonparametric association between e.g. link flow and delay, or signal green share and queue, robust to outliers and nonlinearity; complement to Pearson in regress.
does: Spearman (and Kendall) correlation between two columns of run data
notes: Pearson only today.

idea: Welch two-sample t with Satterthwaite df (Eq 2.13-2.15), pooled-variance t (2.16), two-proportion z test and F-test for equality of variances, for comparing independent sets of runs (different seed sets, or an experiment vs a field/calibration sample) where pairing is impossible; F-test shows whether a design changes reliability (variance), not only the mean.
does: Independent two-sample tests of mean, proportion and variance with CI of the difference
inputs: two lists of values (e.g. per-vehicle times or per-seed KPIs)
notes: Variance comparison is the new part: travel-time reliability between scenarios.

idea: Distribution-free tests for skewed per-vehicle travel times / delays: sign test, Mann-Whitney U (independent), Wilcoxon signed-rank (paired seeds), Kruskal-Wallis (3+ scenarios), median test; use when n small or normality fails.
does: Mann-Whitney / Wilcoxon / Kruskal-Wallis with normal approximation and tie correction
inputs: two or more samples; paired flag
outputs: U or W or H, z, p, effect size
notes: Pure stdlib (ranks, normal cdf via math.erfc; chi-square sf via incomplete gamma).

idea: Chi-square GOF test of simulated vs observed distributions: e.g. headways vs exponential, arrivals per interval vs Poisson/NB (checks the arrival-pattern generators), vehicle-type split vs OD shares, speed class distributions vs field counts; df = k-1-estimated params.
does: Chi-square test of observed counts against a named distribution or expected counts, merging bins with expected<5
inputs: observations or counts, distribution (poisson, exponential, normal, given probs)
notes: Also a self-test that the demand generator produces the claimed arrival process.

idea: Chi-square CI for a variance/SD (2.1.4) and proportion CIs (2.1.3) in analyse_run, e.g. for share of vehicles stopped or delayed over a threshold.
does: CI for proportions and variances of run metrics
notes: Check whether analyse_run already gives proportion CIs; small.

idea: Add leverage (hat diag h_ii, flag >2p/n), Cook's distance D_i=e_i^2/(p MSE)*h_ii/(1-h_ii)^2, studentised residuals, VIF for multicollinearity, adjusted R2 and standardised coefficients to regress output, so the assistant can tell when a handful of runs drive a fitted relationship (e.g. delay vs demand_scale across an experiment's runs).
does: Outlier/influence and collinearity diagnostics for regress
outputs: per-observation h_ii, Cook D, flagged rows, VIF per regressor, adj R2
notes: Needs matrix inverse in pure Python (regress already solves normal equations). Book's advice to document, not drop, outliers is a good LLM-agent rule.

idea: Let regress take log/sqrt transforms, indicator variables for scenario and interaction terms (demand_scale x scenario) so the assistant can test whether a design changes the demand-delay slope (BPR-like curve), not just the level.
does: Transform and interaction options in regress; compares slopes between designs
notes: Dummy encoding of scenario is the key use.

idea: Exhaustive best-subsets and stepwise selection by adj R2/AIC over candidate regressors of run outcomes, with caution that selection is mechanical.
does: Rank regressor subsets
notes: Low priority: assistant has few regressors.

idea: Granger test (Eq 3.59-3.60): regress Y_t on lags of Y and X (unrestricted) vs lags of Y only (restricted), F-test on the lagged-X block, both directions, several lag counts m. Applied to per-minute series of one run: does queue on road A lead queue on B (spillback propagation), does a signal override / TSP request precede delay change, does inflow lead density.
does: Tests temporal precedence between two run series with F-tests for lag counts 1..m
inputs: run id, two series (road flow/queue/speed, throughput, on_road), lags
outputs: F, p each direction, verdict (X->Y, Y->X, both, none)
notes: Needs detector/series from read_detectors; evidence only, not proof; book says test several m. Good explanation aid for the LLM diagnosing where congestion starts.

idea: Vehicles still on the road at run end (or never departed) have right-censored trip times; Tobit/censored-MLE (Eq 3.61) or Kaplan-Meier style handling avoids the downward bias of averaging only completed trips, which matters near saturation.
does: Reports share of censored trips and a censoring-corrected mean travel time
outputs: completed vs unfinished count, naive vs corrected mean, warning when bias large
notes: Complements MSER warm-up; compare experiments fairly when one design leaves more vehicles stuck.

idea: Elasticity e=beta*X/Y (Eq 3.65, Table 3.9 for linear/log-linear/linear-log/double-log) as dimensionless sensitivity of delay/speed to demand, green split, lane count; Box-Cox lambda (Eq 3.62-3.64, Table 3.8) to choose functional form of the delay-vs-demand curve.
does: Fits double-log (and Box-Cox) of outcome vs demand_scale across experiment runs and reports elasticity with CI
notes: Direct what-if sensitivity language for the assistant: a 10% demand rise gives X% delay rise.

idea: Chapter 4 checks: Breusch-Pagan/White test and weighted least squares for non-constant variance (delay variance grows with demand); Durbin-Watson and Cochrane-Orcutt/AR(1) correction for autocorrelated residuals when regressing time series from one run.
does: Runs BP and DW tests on regress residuals, suggests WLS or robust SE
notes: Rising variance with load is almost certain in traffic data; White robust SEs are the cheap fix.

idea: Treat an experiment as panel data: units i = roads/junctions/OD pairs (or seeds), time t = intervals/scenarios. Fixed-effects (within/LSDV, Eq 6.3) removes unobserved unit heterogeneity (a road's geometry) so the scenario effect is estimated within each road; Chow F test (Eq 6.4) for whether unit effects matter; random-effects variance components (sigma_u^2, sigma_v^2) give an intraclass correlation; Hausman test chooses between them.
does: Within-unit estimate of a design's effect on per-road metric (speed, delay, queue) across scenarios with unit fixed effects and cluster-aware SE
inputs: experiment id, metric per road per scenario per seed
outputs: scenario effect, SE, Chow F, ICC, Hausman verdict
notes: Gives per-road/per-junction KPI inference that not_built.md lists as missing; ignoring serial correlation inflates t (book 6.1).

idea: Test whether a design effect differs by group (slopes vary by road class/junction type): fixed/random coefficient model Eq 6.8, i.e. interaction of scenario with group.
does: Tests slope heterogeneity of treatment across road classes
notes: Likely fold into panel_effect_estimate.

idea: Hold out the last k intervals of a run series, forecast with several models, and score ME, MAD, RMSE, SDE, MPE, MAPE (Table 7.4) so the assistant reports how much to trust forecast() and picks the best of moving average (7.1), exponential smoothing, AR(p), seasonal naive.
does: Rolling-origin backtest and model comparison table for run series
inputs: run id, series name, horizon, models
outputs: error table per model, best model, forecast with interval
existing: partial: forecast (Holt only, no accuracy report)
notes: MAPE needs non-zero actuals; use MAD/RMSE for counts near zero.

idea: ACF/PACF of a run series to detect cycles (signal cycle length, bus headway) and pick AR order; fit AR(p)/ARIMA(p,d,q) by least squares/Yule-Walker as an alternative forecaster; Box-Jenkins identify-estimate-check loop (7.3.1-7.3.2).
does: ACF, PACF, Ljung-Box and AR(p) fit with forecast
outputs: ACF/PACF values, dominant period, AR coefficients, Ljung-Box p
notes: Dominant period from ACF would diagnose unintended signal-cycle oscillations or platooning.

idea: State-space model (Eq 7.45) with Kalman filter for short-term traffic state tracking and forecasting from noisy detector data with missing values; also feeds a live LLM agent a smoothed queue/speed estimate.
does: Local-level/trend Kalman filter with forecast standard errors
notes: statistics_catalogue already lists Kalman as not built; local-level model is ~30 lines.

idea: Threshold AR (Eq 7.32) and Markov regime switching (7.43) to model free-flow vs congested regimes; ARCH/GARCH (7.36-7.39) for variance that grows with level (volatility of speed rises as flow rises), a reliability indicator.
does: Fits two-regime threshold AR to speed or flow series, reports regime shares
notes: Speculative; congested/free split is already visible via MSER and cluster_conditions.

idea: PCA on the standardised correlation matrix of KPIs across runs/scenarios/roads (Eq 8.3-8.6: eigenvalues are component variances, proportion j = lambda_j/p): reduces many correlated KPIs (delay, stops, speed, queue, TTC conflicts) to 1-3 interpretable axes (congestion, safety), ranks scenarios on the first axis and detects which KPIs are redundant.
does: Principal components with loadings and scores for scenario or road KPI table
inputs: experiment id or list of KPI rows
outputs: eigenvalues, variance explained, loadings, scores per scenario/road
notes: Pure Python Jacobi eigen solver; complements cluster_conditions (k-means). Factor analysis/SEM in 8.2-8.3 judged too heavy/survey-oriented.

topic: Hazard and survival functions of durations
idea: Hazard h(t)=f/(1-F), survivor S(t)=exp(-H(t)) (Eq 9.1-9.5) applied to simulated durations: time a minor-road vehicle waits for an acceptable gap, queue/jam persistence, stop duration, bus dwell, time until a vehicle gets a green; duration dependence shows whether waits get worse the longer a vehicle has already waited (starvation).
does: Kaplan-Meier survivor curve and empirical hazard of wait/stop/queue durations with right-censoring of vehicles still waiting at run end
inputs: run id, duration type (wait at stop line, stopped time, queue), group
outputs: S(t) table, median, hazard shape, censoring share
notes: Needs per-vehicle events from results; also addresses not_built 'impatience in gap acceptance' diagnosis.

idea: Fit Weibull (Eq 9.15-9.16: shape >1 rising hazard, <1 falling, =1 exponential) and log-logistic hazards, with covariates (queue length, approach flow, conflicting flow) via exp(beta X), to wait-time-for-gap or red-wait data; Cox partial likelihood (Eq 9.10-9.11) when the baseline is unknown; compare models by the Weibull-shape test and LL. Kaplan-Meier product-limit (Eq 9.9) with right censoring is the nonparametric baseline.
does: Weibull/Cox regression of waiting durations on traffic covariates with censoring
outputs: shape parameter, covariate effects (hazard ratios), median wait, fit
notes: Build only after duration_analysis; Newton-Raphson ML in pure Python is doable. Mostly informs a gap-acceptance impatience diagnosis.

idea: Rules from 9.2-9.3: left/right censoring, ties, Kaplan-Meier undefined past a censored max and median undefined if >50% censored; independence of censoring assumption. Use as guard-rails when the assistant reports mean durations from runs where vehicles are still waiting at the end.
does: Guard-rails inside duration_analysis (already logged)
notes: Merge with SRC_020-021 idea.

idea: Extend analyse_safety's SPF: zero-inflated Poisson/NB (Eq 10.18-10.19) for roads with many zero conflicts, Vuong non-nested test (Eq 10.20-10.21) with the decision Table 10.5 (NB overdispersion t vs Vuong V) to choose Poisson/NB/ZIP/ZINB; goodness of fit by likelihood ratio (10.8), deviance G2 (10.9), Rp2 (10.10) and rho2 (10.11); elasticities (10.5) and pseudo-elasticities exp(b)-1)/exp(b) (10.6) of conflict frequency to flow, length, speed, lanes.
does: Fits candidate count models to per-road conflict counts and picks one with GOF and elasticities
inputs: run id or experiment id (road conflict counts, flow, length)
outputs: model table (LL, G2, AIC, Vuong), chosen model, elasticities
notes: Book warns zero-inflation needs a prior reason for a perfectly safe state; in a simulator, low-flow roads justify it. Elasticities give design guidance (a 10% flow rise changes conflicts by X%).

idea: Truncated (zero-excluded) Poisson (10.3) and recursive Poisson probabilities P_j=P_{j-1}*mu/j (Eq 10.7) for counts that cannot be zero (vehicles per platoon, stopped vehicles per cycle).
does: Fit zero-truncated counts
notes: Low priority.

idea: Compute aggregate shares by sample enumeration (average each traveller's probability, Eq 11.44) rather than plugging mean attributes into the logit; the book's route-choice example shows shares 0.152/0.794/0.053 at mean X vs 0.218/0.684/0.098 enumerated (observed 0.219/0.682/0.099). In ACMS: choose_modes and institution_mode_split should draw each trip's distance/time/cost from its distribution (per-institution catchment, per OD pair) and average the probabilities.
does: Mode shares by averaging individual logit probabilities over a sample of travellers/distances, reports aggregation bias versus mean-attribute shares
inputs: OD pair or institution, utility coefficients, sample size
outputs: shares by enumeration, shares at mean, bias per mode
notes: Deterministic and cheap; check how institutions.py computes shares today (likely at one attribute value per institution).

topic: Logit goodness of fit, tests and elasticities
idea: MNL evaluation: likelihood ratio test X2=2[LL(R)-LL(U)] (Eq 11.30), rho2=1-LL(b)/LL(0) and corrected rho2 (11.31-11.32), direct elasticity E=(1-P_i)*beta*x (11.33-11.34) and cross-elasticity -P_j*beta*x. Lets the assistant say how sensitive mode share is to time/cost/headway, and estimate coefficients from observed shares/counts.
does: Elasticities and pseudo-R2 for the mode choice model; MLE fit of coefficients to observed trips with LR test
notes: Elasticity part is S effort; calibration of utilities from observed data is M.

topic: IIA check and richer choice models
idea: IIA property (Eq 11.38: P1/P2 independent of other alternatives) means adding a similar mode (second bus line, bike share) wrongly steals share proportionally (red bus/blue bus problem); remedies are nested logit and mixed logit (Eq 11.53, random coefficients) and probit (Eq 11.8). Add a warning in choose_modes when close substitutes exist and an optional nested structure (public transport nest).
does: Nested logit with a transit nest and logsum; IIA warning
inputs: vehicle types, nest membership, nesting parameter
notes: statistics_catalogue lists probit and mixed logit as unbuilt; nested logit not listed.

idea: Compensating variation CV=(1/mu)[ln sum exp(V_f) - ln sum exp(V_0)] (Eq 11.51), mu = cost coefficient: monetised user benefit of a design change (new bus stop, TSP, signal retiming) from the mode/route choice model, as an economic KPI in experiment comparisons.
does: Per-traveller and total consumer surplus change between baseline and scenario
inputs: experiment id (before/after times and costs), cost coefficient
outputs: CV per person, total per day
notes: Needs value-of-time assumption; a rare KPI that integrates mode shift.

idea: Ordered probit/logit (11.9) for ordered outcomes, e.g. conflict severity classes (minor/serious/severe) or level of service A-F as a function of flow and geometry.
does: Ordered logit of severity or LOS class on covariates
notes: Low priority.

idea: Chi-square test of independence/homogeneity on an I x J table (Eq A.27, df (I-1)(J-1), warning when expected cells are small): e.g. conflict type by scenario, vehicle type by stop/not-stop, mode by institution, lane-change outcome by design; tells whether a design changes the distribution of categorical outcomes, not just a mean.
does: Chi-square independence test with expected counts, standardised residuals and Cramer's V
inputs: table of counts or two categorical columns
outputs: chi2, df, p, cells driving the result
notes: Share chi-square survival function code with goodness_of_fit.

idea: Selectivity bias (Ch12 12.1, Fig 12.1): comparing outcomes of self-selected groups (e.g. vehicles that chose a route, buses that requested TSP) biases effect estimates; use instrumental variables or a selection correction; an agent-explanation rule: do not estimate TSP benefit by comparing buses that got priority with those that did not unless assignment is random or paired by seed.
does: Rule/guard for experiments with self-selected treatment; suggests paired seeded runs
notes: Documentation/prompt guard only.
